Subject: Novalign: EU exit clause and MSA - regulatory annex review

Ben / Laura,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our initial set of redlines to the DPA and the MSA regulatory annex (Novalign_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf). The main items we flagged are:
- EU export / "exit" language around customer data portability and operator assistance on data egress;
- SCC augmentation for UK-specific provisions (post‑Brexit crossover);
- an explicit carve-out for private deployments / on‑prem customer instances; and
- retention and training-data carveouts for safety review.

Procurement is asking for a short summary of the legal position on whether these redlines require a separate transfer-impact addendum or can be addressed as annotated changes to the MSA / DPA. Can someone on your side confirm next steps and a realistic timeline? We may need an internal signoff path for the procurement team next week.

Also looping in Samir (legal) and our procurement counterpart. Attachments: Novalign_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf (redline PDF).

Best,
Elena
Contracts Manager, Novalign Health

Subject: Re: Novalign: EU exit clause and MSA - regulatory annex review

Ben / team / Elena —

I reviewed Novalign_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf and put together high‑level legal comments (attached: Draft_legal_comments.docx). Summary of the principal positions:
1) Exit / egress: suggest adding explicit operator assistance language (reasonable assistance timeframe + costs) rather than an absolute obligation to deliver a full export in all circumstances. Keeps operational risk limited while addressing customer need.
2) SCCs: we should adopt the latest EU SCCs as baseline and add a short UK addendum. That can be handled as a single transfer‑impact addendum (TIA) tied to the DPA — recommended.
3) Private/On‑prem carve-out: acceptable with a scoped definition ("Private Deployment" means customer‑managed infra where Redwood has no remote access except for emergency support). Draft language included.
4) Training data retention: push back on any permanent retention carve‑outs; propose limited retention for safety review with deletion timelines and audit logs.

Next steps I recommend:
- Internal review: Laura to finalize legal comments by 8/20 EOD.
- Privacy evidence ask: Priyom to produce checklist of evidence items we need for SCC/TIA (subprocessors, KMS, data flow diagrams).
- Customer call: propose Wed 8/20 10:30‑11:00 PT to walk redlines.

If Novalign is willing to sign a TIA, that resolves the SCC/UK language in a clean package and procurement will be happy. Attach: Draft_legal_comments.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Ben / Elena —

I reviewed the redlines with infra/privacy. Short technical notes and evidence ask below:
- KMS: confirm key management location (cloud region + managed KMS vs customer‑owned HSM). If customer expects keys to be in‑region, we'll need to validate supported regions.
- Subprocessors: we need a current subprocessor roster and anticipated planned subprocessors for the next 12 months.
- Data flows: a simple diagram showing flows from EU/UK customers to our hosted + dedicated pools will speed the TIA.
- Retention/training data: propose specific retention windows (30 / 90 / 365 days options) and a toggle in the order form for training opt‑out.

I've put an evidence checklist into Privacy_evidence_checklist.xlsx (attached). Also added a short template for the TIA that matches our standard approach — we'll auto‑populate once we get the subproc roster.
